clue.text: As new settler I am going one way and another to get permit

parts.note: I am contracts to I'M

indicators.note: the contraction is written forwards and then once more running the other way, backwards

parts.note: I am contracts to I'M
to permit is to grant, allow

explanation.surface: Someone newly arrived in a country goes back and forth trying to obtain a residence permit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one way and another' turns the second copy of 'I am' round, so the contraction appears forwards then backwards; 'going' and 'to get' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An immigrant is a person who has come to live permanently in a foreign country, a newcomer settling there.

clue.text: Walrus left with very little to eat

parts.note: morse is an old word for the walrus

explanation.surface: A walrus is left with hardly any food.
explanation.walkthrough: MORSE is an archaic name for the walrus, from Finnish/Russian; the surface hopes you think of the Arctic animal's diet.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a tiny mouthful of food, a scrap or bite.

clue.text: Girl sitting in home, an Asian

indicators.note: the girl sits in place right after the word for home, settled next to it

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
Di is a short girl's name, as in Diana

explanation.surface: A girl sits at home with someone from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home' gives IN as in 'staying in'; 'sitting in' places the girl right after it rather than inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of India, the large country of South Asia, is one kind of Asian person.

clue.text: What sports shop sells in illegal enterprise

definitions.meaning: a bat strung for tennis, squash or badminton, stocked in sports shops
a fraudulent scheme or dishonest business, such as a protection scam

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the strung bat used in tennis and a dishonest money-making scheme.

clue.text: Fool on journey from compound

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next, so the fool word comes above the journey word

parts.note: a nit is a fool, a nitwit
a ride is a journey, a trip in a vehicle or on horseback

explanation.surface: A foolish traveller returns from a trip somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word; the definition is 'compound', the chemistry sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitride is a chemical compound of nitrogen with another element, a binary compound in chemistry.

clue.text: One puts pen to paper when there's pressure

definitions.text: One puts pen to paper when there's pressure

parts.words: One puts pen to paper when there's pressure
parts.note: reads like a writer who works only under stress, but describes a recording instrument whose stylus traces atmospheric pressure onto a paper chart

explanation.definitionFit: A barograph is a barometer that records air pressure continuously on a rotating paper drum with a pen.

clue.text: Tour Santa arranged as traveller whizzing miles overhead

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Santa organises a tour, travelling at speed high above the ground on his sleigh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges TOUR SANTA; 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaceman orbits far above the earth at great speed, so is a traveller whizzing miles overhead.

clue.text: Taken up lino, red, falling to bits

indicators.note: something falling to bits breaks apart, so the letters of these three words are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Red linoleum has been pulled up from the floor and is disintegrating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling to bits' rearranges UP LINO RED, which reads as a description of the floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Purloined means stolen, taken without permission.

clue.text: Name idiot having gold as capital

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person, an idiot
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone names a fool who has money as a major asset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' and 'as' are link words; 'capital' looks like money but is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau is the capital city of the Bahamas.

clue.text: Part of the sentence given to a subject

definitions.text: Part of the sentence given to a subject

parts.words: Part of the sentence given to a subject
parts.note: sounds like a prison term handed to a citizen, but in grammar it is the part of a sentence that says something about its subject

explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, this is the portion of a clause containing the verb and stating something about the subject.

clue.text: Bishop covered in black stuff from pen

indicators.note: the bishop is covered by, so placed inside, the black stuff

parts.note: coal is black fuel dug from the ground
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop gets covered in soot from a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title. 'pen' is an animal enclosure, not a writing tool; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A corral is an enclosure for livestock, a pen for horses or cattle.

clue.text: Blokes terrribly eager I found to be a lot of beasts

parts.note: blokes are men

indicators.note: 'to' puts one piece inside the other
terribly suggests a wrecked state, so the letters of eager are mixed up

explanation.surface: Men who are terribly keen form a collection of wild animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrribly' (printed with three Rs) rearranges EAGER into AGER; 'found to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept for exhibition, a zoo.

clue.text: Engineer briefly attracted to one oil-rich area

indicators.note: a word said briefly loses its final letter

parts.note: Isambard Kingdom Brunel was the great Victorian British engineer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An engineer is briefly drawn to an area rich in oil.
explanation.walkthrough: BRUNEL, the Victorian engineer who built the Great Western Railway, is cut short by 'briefly' to BRUNE, and I joins it; 'attracted to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small sultanate on Borneo whose wealth comes from oil and gas reserves.

clue.text: One's outburst makes it hard to see a way ahead

definitions.text: One's outburst makes it hard to see a way ahead

parts.words: One's outburst makes it hard to see a way ahead
parts.note: reads like someone's temper tantrum clouding judgement, but literally describes a device that bursts and releases a screen of fumes

explanation.definitionFit: A canister that bursts to release thick fumes, obscuring vision as a screen in battle or riot control.

clue.text: Support one national organisation's spokesperson

parts.note: a prop is a support
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: Backing a national body's official speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: NT stands for the National Trust, Britain's heritage and countryside conservation charity.
explanation.definitionFit: A proponent is an advocate who speaks up for a cause, so a spokesperson for it.

clue.text: Maybe Cheshire's important person!

definitions.meaning: Cheshire is a large crumbly English cheese, so maybe a big one of those
a VIP or bigwig, someone of influence

explanation.definitionFit: Literally a large cheese such as Cheshire; idiomatically, a powerful or self-important person, a bigwig.

clue.text: Garden attendants waiting to go in, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear marks a word as spoken, sound alike but spelt differently

parts.note: people in a line waiting to be admitted form a queue

explanation.surface: Visitors queue to enter a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in west London; the line of waiting visitors, QUEUE, is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Kew is the celebrated botanic garden in London, home of the Royal Botanic Gardens.

clue.text: One appearing in knight's gear

indicators.note: the numeral appears inside the knight's abbreviation, placed in it

parts.note: Kt is the abbreviation for knight
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone shows up wearing a knight's armour.
explanation.walkthrough: KT is the usual abbreviation of knight (as in honours lists); I goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kit is equipment, the set of clothing and tools for an activity.

clue.text: One hears 'whisky' when bitter is wanted!

indicators.note: one hears marks the word as spoken, sounding the same as the entry but spelt otherwise

parts.note: rye is a whisky distilled from rye grain

explanation.surface: Someone hears a call for whisky when they asked for a bitter beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' looks like the beer but is the definition; 'when ... is wanted' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Wry humour is dry and sardonic, with a bitter twist.

clue.text: Something driven without skill? It's the drink!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the car goes round the skill

parts.note: a Mini is a small car, something you drive
art is skill, craft

explanation.surface: A clumsy driver is told that drinking explains it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old sense 'outside'. The Mini is the classic small British car.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth.

clue.text: Quiet workers united in exceptional joy

indicators.note: the quiet and the workers go inside the word for exceptional

parts.note: something exceptional is rare
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
TU is a trade union, workers united

explanation.surface: Unionised workers quietly share an exceptional happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet; 'workers united' is a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapture is intense delight, ecstatic happiness.

clue.text: Conservative not right to fiddle

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letter for right

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Tory who is not on the right of the party fiddles with policy.
explanation.walkthrough: TORY loses its R; 'to' is a link word, and 'fiddle' is a verb, to play idly.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with something is to fiddle or play with it idly.

clue.text: To argue could engender great disapproval

indicators.note: the words could produce, generate something new when their letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Arguing may stir up strong objection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could engender' rearranges TO ARGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is fierce anger and indignation at something considered wrong, strong condemnation.

clue.text: Money game's beginning with kiss

parts.note: KO is kick-off, the start of a football match
a peck is a quick kiss

explanation.surface: Money starts the game, with a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: KO is the usual abbreviation for kick-off, the start of a football game.
explanation.definitionFit: A kopeck is a Russian coin, a hundredth of a rouble.

clue.text: Plan various matches with time running out

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of matches are mixed up, with time running out of them

explanation.surface: Organise several fixtures before the clock runs down.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange MATCHES ('various') and let T ('time') run out of it, leaving SCHEMA; 'running out' says the T goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A schema is an outline or diagrammatic plan.

clue.text: Special look at compass

parts.note: to read is to look at a text

explanation.surface: Inspect a special compass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compass' means range or extent, not the direction-finding instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass in the sense of range or scope matches a spread, the extent of something.

clue.text: Hand conceals pound, gold coin

indicators.note: the hand word hides the pound and gold inside it

parts.note: fin is slang for a hand
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra
or is heraldic gold

explanation.surface: Someone's hand hides a pound and a gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: FIN is old slang for a hand; L is from Latin libra and OR is heraldic gold. The florin was the British two-shilling coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The florin was a British two-shilling coin, and earlier a gold coin of Florence.

clue.text: Collection left in pocket is redistributed

indicators.note: redistributed suggests sharing out again, so the letters are dealt into a new order

explanation.surface: A hoard kept in a pocket is shared out again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redistributed' rearranges the abbreviation for 'left' along with the next two words; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockpile is a large accumulated supply, a hoard or collection of goods.

clue.text: What gets men plastered finally, immersed in drink?

definitions.text: What gets men plastered finally, immersed in drink?

indicators.note: the final letters are immersed in, so placed inside, the drink

parts.note: beer is a drink

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Asks what makes men drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters of 'men' and 'plastered', N and D, are dunked in BEER. The whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bender is a drinking spree, a bout of heavy boozing that leaves people drunk.

clue.text: Feel encouraged to follow in Dracula's footsteps?

definitions.meaning: a whimsical literal reading: seize a victim's vital organ, as a vampire might

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be heartened; read literally, it is seizing someone's cardiac organ, like a bloodthirsty vampire.

clue.text: Second English architect employed by Aussie university

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
John Nash designed Regency London, including Regent Street

explanation.surface: An English architect is briefly taken on by an Australian university.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is short for a moment; John Nash was the Regency architect behind Regent's Park terraces and Brighton Pavilion. 'employed by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Monash University is a large university in Melbourne, Australia.

clue.text: Plant and animal in the pictures mum put out

indicators.note: the animal goes inside what remains of the picture house word
mum is put out, ejected from the picture house word

parts.note: the pictures is the cinema
ma is mum
an eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A plant and an animal appear in a film after mum walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' removes mum from the picture house word, leaving CINE, and 'in' puts the antelope inside; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The celandine is a small yellow-flowered plant of the buttercup or poppy family.
